questions.q: Why did Captain Hoseason call Alan and David out of the round-house late at night?
choices: He wanted them to help pilot the brig because it was in danger
He wanted to make peace with them and share a drink before landing
He had spotted a ship of red-coats coming up behind them
He needed them to help nurse the sailors wounded in the fight
questions.evidence: come out and see if ye can pilot

questions.q: What did the "fountain" rising out of the moonlit sea turn out to be?
choices: A whale blowing near the ship
The sea breaking on a reef
Spray from a hidden waterfall
A signal rocket from the shore
questions.evidence: The sea breaking on a reef

questions.q: What name did Alan think the dangerous reefs were called?
choices: The Rocks of Iona
The Torran Rocks
The Ross of Mull
The Teeth of Earraid
questions.evidence: these'll be what they call the Torran Rocks

questions.q: Hoseason says he would never risk his brig "in sic a stoneyard." What does he mean by a "stoneyard"?
choices: A harbour with a stone pier
A sea full of rocks and reefs
A quarry on the island shore
A graveyard for drowned sailors
questions.evidence: risk my brig in sic a stoneyard

questions.q: Where did Alan remember the water was clearer of reefs?
choices: Out to the south, in the open sea
Close in under the land
Far out to the west of Tiree
Straight through the Sound of Mull
questions.evidence: it is clearer under the land

questions.q: What was Mr. Riach's job while the brig sailed through the reefs?
choices: He steered the brig with the help of two seamen
He sat aloft in the foretop calling out what he saw
He stood in the bow measuring the depth with a line
He guarded the round-house to keep Alan from escaping

questions.q: What did David come to think of the captain and Mr. Riach as they worked through the reefs?
choices: That they were cowards in battle and just as cowardly at sea
That they were brave and steady in their own trade
That they were only pretending to be in danger
That they cared more for the gold than the brig
questions.evidence: I saw they were brave in their own trade

questions.q: How did Alan feel as the brig passed so close to the reefs?
choices: He was white and did not like the idea of such a cold death
He was cheerful and sang songs to keep up the crew's courage
He was angry that the captain had not bought a proper chart
He was calm and bored, since he had sailed there many times
questions.evidence: this is no the kind of death I fancy

questions.q: What happened just after Hoseason told Alan, "Ye have saved the brig, sir"?
choices: The brig sailed safely into Linnhe Loch
The crew turned on Alan and tried to seize his belt
The tide caught the brig and it struck a reef
Mr. Riach fell from the mast into the sea
questions.evidence: struck the reef with such a dunch as threw us all flat upon the deck

questions.q: Near which little isle did the brig strike the reef?
choices: Iona
Tiree
Earraid
Canna
questions.evidence: off a little isle they call Earraid

questions.q: What did Captain Hoseason do while the men worked to launch the skiff?
choices: He gave sharp orders and worked hardest of all
He stood holding the shrouds, groaning and talking to himself
He rowed away alone in the skiff before it was ready
He went below to save his papers and money from the cabin
questions.evidence: He stood holding by the shrouds, talking to himself and groaning

questions.q: What did Alan say about the country on the shore near the wreck?
choices: It was a land of the Campbells, the worst place for him
It was his own country of Appin, full of friends
It was an empty island where no one had ever lived
It was the King's land, guarded day and night by many red-coat soldiers
questions.evidence: it was a land of the Campbells

questions.q: How did David end up in the sea?
choices: He jumped over to swim for the shore
A huge sea tilted the ship and threw him over
A sailor pushed him over during the confusion
The skiff he was sitting in turned over in the heavy waves
questions.evidence: I was cast clean over the bulwarks into the sea

questions.q: What does David later understand had carried him so quickly away from the brig?
choices: A strong wind that blew him over the waves
A roost, or tide race, in the water
A sea serpent he glimpsed in the moonlight
Alan towing him with an oar
questions.evidence: it must have been the roost or tide race

questions.q: Since David could not swim, how did he reach the shore?
choices: He held the spare yard and kicked with his feet
A fisherman in a small boat pulled him in
The waves washed him onto the sand while he slept
He grabbed a rope that Alan threw to him
questions.evidence: when I laid hold upon the yard with both arms, and kicked out with both feet

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Alan and David fighting off a second attack by the crew
The brig hitting a reef and David washing ashore alone
The captain putting Alan and David ashore on the Isle of Mull
David learning how to sail the brig at night
questions.evidence: I cannot tell if I was more tired or more grateful
